subject: Follow-up: HealthCore audit log scope & next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@healthcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: HealthCore audit log scope & next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on requirements for audit logging and compliance scope.

Call highlights (TL;DR):
- Primary compliance drivers: HIPAA (PHI handling), SOC 2 report for procurement, and GDPR for EU-born patient data.
- Desired audit coverage: admin activity (user creation/role changes), API request logs (requests + identities + response status), model-inference trace (request id + timestamps), and data export records.
- Retention target: 7 years for specific PHI-related events (per your policy), 12 months standard for non-PHI operational logs — we discussed export/WORM options.

Open clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Do you require our SOC 2 Type II report or just the bridge/summary for now?
2) Will HealthCore's procurement team require a signed BAA?
3) For immutability you mentioned object-locking on exported logs — do you prefer S3 Object Lock (governance/compliance mode) or an on-prem archival option?

What I can do this week:
- Share our audit-log export capabilities doc (JSONL + zipped manifests) and a sample schema for admin/API entries.
- Kick off the vendor security questionnaire (VSAQ) and send you a spreadsheet to collect technical controls.
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with one of our infra engineers to walk through retention/ immutability patterns (recommended).

Next steps/asks for HealthCore:
- Please confirm SOC 2/Baa expectations and the primary contact for procurement.
- Send any minimal required log fields we must include for your audit (e.g., patient-id pseudonymization policy).

Attachments: call-recording-20270215.m4a (we recorded the call), placeholder: HealthCore-VSAQ-template.xlsx (I'll attach the VSAQ template in my next email).

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@healthcore.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCore Security Team <security@healthcore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 17:28:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: HealthCore audit log scope & next steps

Thanks Vivek — appreciated the summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement will need a SOC 2 Type II report; for initial evaluation, a SOC 2 bridge letter + expected date for the full report is acceptable.
- Yes, we will require a signed BAA (HIPAA). Legal can provide the contact; cc'd our security inbox.
- For immutability: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode is our preferred cloud option. On-prem archival is a fallback if Object Lock can't be demonstrated. We also want an integrity manifest with SHA256 checksums for each exported file.

Audit fields we care about (minimal set):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_id (internal user id / service principal)
- actor_role
- action (create/update/delete/login/role_change/api_call)
- resource_type and resource_id
- request_id (trace id)
- response_code or outcome
- originating_ip (for admin console/API calls)

We'll send you a short checklist from Legal but please include the VSAQ so we can start filling it in. Also please confirm whether exports include request/response hashes or just request metadata (we prefer hashes for integrity).

— Aisha
Aisha Patel
Director, Infrastructure Security | HealthCore
aisha.patel@healthcore.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@healthcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, HealthCore Security Team <security@healthcore.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:05:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: HealthCore audit log scope & next steps

Great — thanks for the specifics, Aisha. Answers inline and next steps below.

- SOC 2: we can provide a current SOC 2 Type II report PDF and a short bridge letter describing scope differences. I'll pull the latest report and share a link (redacted) with Legal.
- BAA: we do execute BAAs. I'll loop in our legal ops once you share your counterparty contact.
- Immutability/Exports: we support the following options today:
  * Direct S3 export (JSONL), with optional S3 Object Lock (Compliance mode) and versioned manifests. Exports include a companion manifest.jsonl.gz with SHA256 checksums and export metadata (export start/end time, total objects, sequence ranges).
  * WORM archives via partner-managed vaults for long-term retention (1–7+ years).
  * Live streaming export (syslog/CEF) to a customer collector for near real-time ingestion.
  * Programmatic retrieval: GET /v1/audit/logs?start=<ISO>&end=<ISO>&format=jsonl returns paged, signed manifests; each page contains request hashes and monotonic offsets for rebuildability.

- Audit coverage: admin activity logs and API request logs include actor identity, role, IP, request_id, timestamp, and a response summary. We also produce a model-inference trace that links request_id -> model_version -> token_count, but inference payloads do not contain raw customer data unless configured to persist.

- Retention: default 365 days for operational logs. For PHI/longer retention we offer customizable retention policies at export time and can configure S3 Object Lock with a retention period you specify.

I've attached a short explainer (redwood-audit-exports.pdf) and the VSAQ template (HealthCore-VSAQ-template.xlsx). I'll also create the shared Drive folder and post the HubSpot deal link.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll upload SOC 2 redacted PDF + bridge letter to the Drive folder by EOD Wed.
2) HealthCore to fill the VSAQ template; we can iterate asynchronously.
3) Schedule a 45-min technical deep dive Friday or early next week with our infra lead to demo exports and Object Lock proof-of-concept.

If that sounds good I'll send calendar invites.

Best — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-audit-exports.pdf, HealthCore-VSAQ-template.xlsx
